evals.prompt: Create a Kotlin Cart aggregate using Wow's Simple Aggregation Pattern. The cart has a maximum capacity of 10 items, AddCartItem emits CartItemAdded or CartQuantityChanged, RemoveCartItem emits CartItemRemoved, and CartItem contains productId and quantity. Write CartState.kt and Cart.kt as fenced, compilable Kotlin.
evals.expected_output: Fenced, compilable CartState.kt and Cart.kt. Descriptively named sourcing and command handlers carry the required discovery annotations; command handlers emit domain events without mutating state directly.

rubric.criterion: Command handlers decide and emit events while state mutation stays in deterministic sourcing handlers.
Every sourcing handler not named exactly onSourcing declares @OnSourcing.
Every command handler not named exactly onCommand declares @OnCommand, so both AddCartItem and RemoveCartItem are discoverable.
The implementation enforces capacity 10, emits CartItemAdded for a new product, CartQuantityChanged for an existing product, and CartItemRemoved for removal.
The fenced Kotlin is internally type-consistent, imports or qualifies required Wow APIs, and can be placed into CartState.kt and Cart.kt without placeholder identifiers.

evals.prompt: Write a Kotlin TransferSaga. Prepared produces Entry for the target account, AmountEntered produces Confirm, and EntryFailed produces UnlockAmount for the source account. Use Wow's stateless Saga conventions and return fenced, compilable Kotlin.
evals.expected_output: Fenced, compilable Kotlin containing a @StatelessSaga with three discoverable event handlers that return fully routed Entry, Confirm, and UnlockAmount commands or command builders.

rubric.criterion: The Saga coordinates commands and does not own aggregate state or invariants.
Each generated command contains or derives the correct target aggregate identity.
Each handler is named exactly onEvent or declares @OnEvent, so all three event-to-command mappings are registered.
The fenced Kotlin is internally type-consistent, imports or qualifies required Wow APIs, and contains no placeholder identifiers.

evals.prompt: Write fenced, compilable Kotlin AggregateSpec tests for Cart: add to an empty cart, add the same product twice, remove an item, and reject adding beyond capacity 10. Use fork() for branches and verify resulting state.
evals.expected_output: Fenced, compilable CartSpec Kotlin using AggregateSpec, fork(), event assertions, an error assertion for capacity, and expectState for sourced state.

rubric.criterion: The four requested paths are independent and include the capacity error boundary.
Assertions prove emitted facts and sourced state, not implementation details.
The tests assert CartItemAdded, CartQuantityChanged, and CartItemRemoved, plus the capacity error path.
The fenced Kotlin is internally type-consistent, imports or qualifies required Wow test APIs, and contains no placeholder identifiers.

evals.prompt: Create Kotlin Order read-model and notification processors. OrderCreated creates an order summary. OrderPaid may represent partial payment, so the projection must take status from the sourced OrderState rather than always writing PAID. Send blocking email only after full payment, outside projection replay, without blocking a Reactor event-loop thread; identify the notification idempotency key. Return fenced, compilable Kotlin snippets.
evals.expected_output: Fenced Kotlin containing a @ProjectionProcessor whose state-event handler writes OrderState.status, plus a separate @EventProcessor whose @Blocking handler accepts DomainEvent<OrderPaid> or DomainEventExchange<OrderPaid>, returns early when body.paid is false, and uses the event message id as the idempotency key.

rubric.criterion: The blocking call is explicitly marked so Wow can move invocation off a Reactor non-blocking thread.
Read-model updates stay in the projection, while external notification is isolated from projection replay in an EventProcessor.
The projection handles OrderCreated and creates the requested order summary.
The projection uses sourced OrderState.status so partial payment does not incorrectly become PAID.

The EventProcessor handler accepts DomainEvent<OrderPaid> or DomainEventExchange<OrderPaid>, returns before the side effect when paid is false, and derives the idempotency key from the event message or exchange rather than the OrderPaid body.
OrderCreated and OrderPaid projection functions are discoverable state-event handlers, and the notification function is a discoverable event handler.
The fenced Kotlin is internally type-consistent, imports or qualifies required Wow APIs, and contains no placeholder identifiers.

evals.prompt: Write fenced, compilable Kotlin using the Wow Query DSL to page ACTIVE orders of one tenant. Sort createdAt descending and project only id, status, and totalAmount.
evals.expected_output: Fenced, compilable Kotlin containing a pagedQuery with tenantId and status conditions, pagination, descending createdAt sort, and an include projection for the requested fields.

rubric.criterion: Filtering, pagination, and sorting use the current Kotlin DSL boundaries. The projection includes only id, status, and totalAmount; one vararg include call and three separate include calls are both valid.
The fenced Kotlin is internally type-consistent, imports or qualifies the current Query DSL APIs, and contains no placeholder identifiers.

evals.prompt: Define a Kotlin @PreparableKey username uniqueness index. The String argument is the username key; the stored value contains userId and password. Show the PrepareKey interface and one usingPrepare call as fenced, compilable Kotlin.
evals.expected_output: Fenced Kotlin where UsernamePrepare or UsernamePrepareKey extends PrepareKey<UsernameIndexValue>; the key argument remains String and usingPrepare receives either an inline UsernameIndexValue or a variable constructed from that type.

rubric.criterion: The generic parameter models the stored value, not the String reservation key.
UsernamePrepare is marked with @PreparableKey so the framework can register the interface.
usingPrepare receives username as the String key and a UsernameIndexValue containing userId and password as its value; a raw String value is invalid.
The fenced Kotlin is internally type-consistent and the usingPrepare call conforms to PrepareKey<UsernameIndexValue>.

evals.prompt: Configure Wow storage routing so Kotlin aggregate HotAggregate uses Redis for both events and snapshots. It has no explicit @Name annotation. Return fenced block-style YAML (not flow mappings) and explain the routing key.
evals.expected_output: Fenced, valid block-style YAML under wow.eventsourcing.storage-routing.aggregates.hot_aggregate with Redis event and snapshot storage, plus an explanation of exact Pascal-to-snake metadata-name matching.

rubric.criterion: The YAML is rooted at the exact wow.eventsourcing.storage-routing configuration prefix, expressed as nested keys or an equivalent dotted key; a similar path in explanatory prose is not sufficient.
The map key is the discovered aggregate metadata name hot_aggregate, not the Kotlin class name.
Event and snapshot channels each select exactly one Redis storage target.
The fenced YAML preserves the configuration hierarchy; matching key tokens listed at unrelated indentation levels is invalid.

evals.prompt: A Kotlin Wow Saga handler is not invoked. Diagnose only; do not modify files. Describe how to prove or disprove Spring bean discovery, Saga function registration, event selection, and bus subscription. Explain the limited role of META-INF/wow-metadata.json and what @Retry can and cannot account for.
evals.expected_output: A read-only, stage-by-stage diagnosis that checks the @StatelessSaga Spring bean, AutoRegistrar and StatelessSagaFunctionRegistrar, function selection and subscription. It explains that wow-metadata.json carries bounded-context and aggregate metadata rather than registering the Saga. It distinguishes selection from invocation: once the dispatcher attaches a matching function to the exchange, EventCompensationFilter may inspect its @Retry for a downstream reactive failure even if the handler body did not run.

rubric.criterion: The plan distinguishes Spring component discovery, function registration, event filtering, and bus subscription.
KSP metadata is limited to bounded-context and aggregate metadata; it is not presented as the Saga bean-registration mechanism.

@Retry is tied to a function already selected and attached to the exchange. EventCompensationFilter can inspect it for a downstream reactive failure before, during, or after function invocation; invocation is not a prerequisite. It cannot explain missing registration, matching, selection, or event delivery.

evals.expected_output: Findings-first review identifies direct command-handler state mutation as a correctness issue and missing focused aggregate behavior/sourcing coverage as a test gap.

rubric.criterion: The review treats direct aggregate state mutation as an event-sourcing correctness problem, not a style preference.
The review requires a focused aggregate test proving the event and sourced state.
